Physiologically based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) model apixaban (body model)
Whole-body physiologically based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) model of apixaban, built with the PBPK library pkpdsim.pbpk: the dissolution of the tablet and the incomplete absorption of apixaban in the intestine, its efflux into the intestinal lumen (P-gp, BCRP), the distribution into the tissues, the metabolism by CYP3A4 in the liver to O-demethyl apixaban (M2), hydroxy apixaban (M7) and O-demethyl apixaban sulfate (M1), the renal excretion of apixaban, M1 and M7 and the biliary excretion of the metabolites, and the anticoagulant effects (anti-factor Xa activity, INR, PT, mPT, aPTT) of the total apixaban concentration of the plasma, with the effects of impaired renal and hepatic function, of the body weight and of the interactions of CYP3A4 and P-gp.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: 1 at 35 years, the age of the individual of a build without the physiology over age (PBPKDefinition.age, which gives the curve of pkpdsim.pbpk.age): the hematocrit (fraction) of a newborn at term: days 0, 7, 14 and 28 of Scholkmann 2019, Equation 2 evaluated as printed at a gestational age of 40 weeks (the fit of about 100 000 neonates of Henry and Christensen 2015); the nadir 0.35 at 2 months of the PK-Sim database (secondary, the source of the value not read); from 1 year the table of NHANES. Jopling 2009 (Intermountain Healthcare, 41 957 hematocrit and 39 559 hemoglobin values of the first 28 days, every patient who received an erythrocyte transfusion excluded) confirms two things read before from its abstract only: there is no effect of sex on the hematocrit or the hemoglobin of the neonate, which the authors state they can now conclude confidently from this sample size, and the fall over the first 28 days, their term group (35-42 weeks) going from a mean hemoglobin of 18 g/dl (5th percentile 14) at birth to 13 g/dl (5th percentile 9.5) at 28 days, a ratio of 0.72 against the 0.385/0.522 = 0.74 of this curve. Their regression of the hematocrit on the gestational age within 6 hours of birth, 28.59 + 0.6359*GA in weeks (25 464 values), gives 54.0 % at 40 weeks against the 52.2 % here, and their reference range of the hematocrit at birth in term neonates is 42 to 65 %. Not modelled: the hematocrit of a late preterm or term neonate rises by 3.6 +- 0.5 % during the first four hours after delivery (placental transfusion), so day 0 is the value within hours of birth; the ratio of the hematocrit of the sex to its value at 35 years (blood_nhanes.toml, 1 to 80 years); the respondents of 80 years and over are placed at 85 years, a model choice (their mean age is not published); constant beyond

body.p: 1 at 35 years, the age of the individual of a build without the physiology over age (PBPKDefinition.age, which gives the curve of pkpdsim.pbpk.age): the global cerebral blood flow per mass relative to the adults (51 ml/min/100 g of 32 adults of 18-29 years), Xe-133 SPECT of 42 neurologically normal children (Table 1: 2-45 days 50, 2-7 months 55, 9-15 months 60, 16-22 months 62, 2-4 years 65, 6-19 years 62 ml/min/100 g, at the middle of each group; the maximum 71 at 5 years and the adult value after 19 years of the text); the brain takes 47 % of the cardiac output at 1 year (Wu 2016: 45.5 % below 4 years by 4D flow MRI, 14.5 % in adults); the fraction of the cardiac output to the liver (hepatic artery and portal organs) follows the liver volume (liver_mass), so the hepatic blood flow is the cardiac output times the liver volume factor, 0.72 at 80 years; a model choice of the form after Imamura 2026. Zoli 1999 Table 1 (40 healthy subjects within 10 % of the ideal body weight, 10 per group, echo-Doppler of the portal vein and the common hepatic artery, functional flow by the hepatic clearance of D-sorbitol) measures, for the age groups below 45, 45-60, 61-75 and above 75 years: portal flow 1209 +- 205, 980 +- 337, 978 +- 194 and 749 +- 117 ml/min (ANOVA p = 0.0018), hepatic artery flow 235 +- 76, 313 +- 117, 318 +- 144 and 271 +- 94 ml/min (p = 0.3632, not significant), total hepatic flow 1445 +- 220, 1293 +- 340, 1297 +- 253 and 1020 +- 148 ml/min (p = 0.0088) and functional hepatic flow 1514 +- 250, 1326 +- 348, 1258 +- 226 and 1015 +- 163 ml/min (p = 0.0023). The total flow above 75 years is 1020/1445 = 0.706 of the flow below 45 years and the functional flow 1015/1514 = 0.670; the two are correlated over the whole population (r = 0.871), so the fall is a fall of the flow and not an intrahepatic shunt. The decline is in the portal limb: the hepatic artery flow does not change significantly (a mild rise between 45 and 75 years), while the library applies one factor to the hepatic artery and the portal organs together, which is a known simplification. The library's factor is also shallower than these data at the oldest ages (0.835 at 80 years against the 0.706 of the group above 75 years), because its form follows the liver volume of Imamura 2026 and is anchored at 50 years; renal plasma flow: 1 to 40 years, -0.012 per year to 85 years (fitted to the effective renal plasma flow of Davies and Shock 1950, men; Fliser 1993 0.52 at 70 against 26 years); beyond 85 years the filtration fraction is held, the flow follows the GFR of men (0.46 * 0.578/0.6796 at 100 years), a model choice: the line would give a filtration fraction of 0.36; no reliable sex difference (Berg 2006, abstract), both sexes alike, held at the filtration fraction of men beyond 85 years; cardiac index at a fixed body surface area: 1 - 0.0030 * (age - 35) (cardiovascular magnetic resonance of Carlsson 2012, -0.21 to -0.29 % per year; the three-dimensional echocardiography of Patel 2021 about -0.25 % per year); both sexes alike; the decline is debated, 1.0 to 0.64 at 80 years in the literature

The total flow above 75 years is 1020/1445 = 0.706 of the flow below 45 years and the functional flow 1015/1514 = 0.670; the two are correlated over the whole population (r = 0.871), so the fall is a fall of the flow and not an intrahepatic shunt. The decline is in the portal limb: the hepatic artery flow does not change significantly (a mild rise between 45 and 75 years), while the library applies one factor to the hepatic artery and the portal organs together, which is a known simplification. The library's factor is also shallower than these data at the oldest ages (0.835 at 80 years against the 0.706 of the group above 75 years), because its form follows the liver volume of Imamura 2026 and is anchored at 50 years; renal plasma flow: 1 to 40 years, -0.012 per year to 85 years (fitted to the effective renal plasma flow of Davies and Shock 1950, men; Fliser 1993 0.52 at 70 against 26 years); beyond 85 years the filtration fraction is held, the flow follows the GFR of men (0.46 * 0.578/0.6796 at 100 years), a model choice: the line would give a filtration fraction of 0.36; no reliable sex difference (Berg 2006, abstract), both sexes alike, held at the filtration fraction of men beyond 85 years; cardiac index at a fixed body surface area: 1 - 0.0030 * (age - 35) (cardiovascular magnetic resonance of Carlsson 2012, -0.21 to -0.29 % per year; the three-dimensional echocardiography of Patel 2021 about -0.25 % per year); both sexes alike; the decline is debated, 1.0 to 0.64 at 80 years in the literature

body.p: The factor of the sex on the cardiac output of the female individual of 35 years relative to a man of the same body weight and height (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): The cardiac index (cardiac output per body surface area) of women and men of the same size is the same: Williams 1994 (the source of the cardiac output of ICRP 89; Table 5, the same reference cardiac index of both sexes at every age, 3.7 l/min/m2 at 24 and 3.6 at 34 years, the 6.5 and 5.9 l/min of the adults the different body sizes), Carlsson 2012 (CMR, n = 144, 3.1 +- 0.4 women and 3.2 +- 0.5 l/min/m2 men, p = 0.64), Patel 2021 (WASE, n = 605, 18-40 years, equal), de Simone 1997 (no sex effect at the same body surface area or weight, children and adults) and Middlemiss 2019 (inert gas rebreathing, n = 600, 20-49 years, women 0.94-0.96 at the same size). The scaling of the cardiac output with the lean tissue of the sex (Huisinga 2012) gives a woman about 9 % more cardiac output than a man of the same body weight and height (women have more cardiac output per fat-free mass, 20-25 % in Middlemiss 2019 and Yeon 2015, and less fat-free mass at the same size); the factor removes it, computed from the physiology at every age of the form same_cardiac_index (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences.same_cardiac_index): the male over the female cardiac output of the scaling at the body weight and height between the reference individuals of the age, linear between the ages; 0.914 of the adults (a direct fit of the library to the 12 groups of Middlemiss 2019 gives 0.911, the range of the evidence 0.88-0.96), near 1 in the children, whose references of ICRP 89 have the same cardiac output in both sexes until 10 years (Williams 1994 p. 14: independent of sex until near 10 years), and removing the drift of the references over puberty; the same in the elderly (no consistent sex difference of the decline: Carlsson 2012, Middlemiss 2019, Williams 1994).

body.p: The factor of the sex on the brain fraction of the cardiac output of the female individual of 35 years relative to a man of the same body weight and height (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): The cerebral blood flow per mass of young women is higher than of men: PET 15O-water +17 % at 20 years and +2 % at 65 years (Aanerud 2017, n = 58, cortical grey matter, Table 1), pCASL +16.5 % (Alisch 2021, n = 80), Xe-133 +11 % at all ages (Rodriguez 1988), and the total cerebral blood flow by phase-contrast MRI is higher despite a smaller brain (Xing 2017, 21-45 years, 724 +- 112 women and 551 +- 111 ml/min men, 21.3 and 14.8 % of the cardiac output); ICRP 89 gives both sexes 12 % of the cardiac output and the same perfusion per mass. The factor on the brain fraction of the cardiac output of the women (the other fractions share the rest in their proportions) gives the perfusion per mass of the female reference individual 1.17 times the male at 18-45 years and 1.02 from 65 years (Aanerud 2017 at 65 years, Smith 2019 -4 % with the hematocrit of each subject, Alisch 2021 70-79 years +3 %), with the factor of the cardiac output: 1.17/0.931 = 1.257 and 1.02/0.931 = 1.096 (0.931 the perfusion ratio of the references with the cardiac output factor alone); 1 until 12 years (no difference before puberty, Satterthwaite 2014, n = 922, 8-22 years, the divergence at mid-puberty, and Wu 2016), the rise over puberty and the fall from 45 to 65 years (the faster decline of the women, Aanerud 2017 -3.8 against -1.0 % per decade) linear, a choice.

body.p: The factor of the sex on the transit time of the stomach in the fed state of the female individual of 35 years relative to a man of the same body weight and height (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): The emptying of a meal (caloric liquids and solids) of premenopausal women is slower than of men: scintigraphy of solids, Camilleri 2012 (n = 319, 127.7 +- 28.7 women and 109.9 +- 28.6 min men, Table 2A, 1.16 of the means and 1.19 of the medians, sex significant after age and BMI) and Vasavid 2014 (n = 189, 1.17); the smaller studies of premenopausal women 1.42-1.78 (Datz 1987, Hutson 1989), rounded to 1.33 (caloric liquids) and 1.40 (solids) by ICRP 89 (para 275); 1.2 of the large cohorts on the fed transit time of the stomach (T_st_fed). The fasted emptying of water does not differ (ICRP 89, 30 min both sexes; no sex difference of the fasting motility). Children before puberty 1 (ICRP 89 children with the values of the men, Hauser 2016 no sex effect at 1-17 years), the difference from puberty (Karrento 2025, n = 216, half time 86.6 girls and 73.6 min boys, 1.18), linear from 10 to 15 years; postmenopausal women without hormone replacement empty solids like men (Hutson 1989, Gryback 2000, Vasavid 2014), linear from 45 to 55 years, a choice.

body.p: The factor of the sex on the transit times of the large intestine of the female individual of 35 years relative to a man of the same body weight and height (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): The colonic transit of women is slower than of men: ICRP 89 para 277, the colonic transit time of the adult females one third greater than of the males (48 and 36 h, 16 and 12 h for each of the right colon, the left colon and the rectosigmoid); radio-opaque markers, Metcalf 1987 (the segmental transits of the library, 35 h of a group of both sexes; the men significantly faster over the whole colon), Meier 1995 (n = 164, 1.40), Degen 1996 (colonic transit faster in men). body.p: 1 at 35 years, the age of the individual of a build without the physiology over age (PBPKDefinition.age, which gives the curve of pkpdsim.pbpk.age): maturation: Table 2, the theoretical allometric model using normal fat mass (923 GFR measurements of 923 subjects from 22 weeks of postmenstrual age to 31 years, inulin, 51Cr-EDTA, 99mTc-DTPA and iohexol): half of the adult GFR at 47.7 weeks of postmenstrual age (95 % CI 45.1-50.5), Hill coefficient 3.40 (3.03-3.80), adult GFR 121 ml/min (117-125). At term (40 weeks of postmenstrual age) the function is 0.354, which is the 35 % of the asymptotic adult value the paper states, and at 1 year of postnatal age the predicted GFR is 90 % of the adult. Sex was not associated with any systematic difference, postnatal age added nothing over postmenstrual age, and the fat-free mass described the size better than the total body weight. The size term of this column is (WT/70)^0.75 while the library scales the GFR with the body surface area; Table 2 also gives the parameters estimated with a body surface area size model, TM50 52.7 weeks (48.9-56.6), Hill 3.30 (2.92-3.78) and an adult GFR of 101 ml/min (97-104), which would be the self-consistent pairing for the library and would make a term newborn 0.287 instead of 0.354 of the adult. The library keeps the normal fat mass column, which is the parameterisation of the paper and of every model derived from it, because Rhodin 2009 judge the body surface area scaling clearly worse and compute the body surface area by the Boyd formula from weight alone (their equation on p. 69), not by the Du Bois formula of the library; the body surface area column is recorded here as the alternative and is not used; aging: as men to 50 years (Delanaye 2022, Pottel 2017); from 50 years the slope of the healthy women of Eriksen 2020 (Table 3), -0.00866 per year; linear, extrapolated beyond 95 years

body.p: GFR of the individual at renal function 1: the reference GFR, which is roughly proportional to body size (ICRP 89 Section 8.3.1), scaled with the body surface area, i.e. the same GFR per 1.73 m2, times the factor of the age fage_GFR (the maturation of the children and the decline of the adults). body.p: The plasma albumin of the female build relative to the men of the same age (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): The plasma albumin of the women is lower than of the men from puberty to about 55 years: NHANES 2013-2018, survey-weighted means, 0.93-0.95 at 18-49 years, 0.98-0.99 from 55 years, 0.997 at 12 years (blood_nhanes.toml), Weaving 2016 (n = 1,079,193, the values of the women close to the men at 60 years); not an effect of the oral contraceptives (NHANES women of 20-49 years without estrogen 0.943). The curve of the women over age is relative to the women of 35 years (age_human.toml); the constant ratio of the women to the men at 35 years, 41.65/44.32 = 0.9398, times it gives the ratio of NHANES at every age from 12 years and 0.997 below, so puberty and the menopause need no switch.

body.p: The activity of CYP3A4 in the liver of the female build relative to the men of the same age, per amount of tissue (pkpdsim.pbpk.sex_differences): Every kind of evidence finds the women higher: the protein of the liver 2.0-2.3-fold by immunoblot (Wolbold 2003, 94 livers; verapamil N-dealkylation +50 %) and 1.18 by LC-MS/MS (Gaither 2025, n = 94, n.s.), the mRNA of GTEx 1.33-1.76, the activity of liver microsomes 1.24-1.55, the P-gp-independent marker 4beta-hydroxycholesterol +21 % (n = 1440, adjusted); midazolam (meta-analysis of Hu and Zhao 2010) oral clearance per kg +16 %, systemic +20 %. With the liver mass and the flows of the female build 1.2 gives +14 % (oral) and +15 % (systemic) per kg, without a factor -5 % and 0 to +4 %; the intestine alike (Paine 2005), the P-gp of liver and intestine alike, so not a P-gp effect (Cummins 2002). No change at the menopause (protein, Wolbold 2003; midazolam, Gorski 2000; erythromycin breath test, Harris 1996; no effect of hormone replacement) and no difference in the children (Parvez 2024).

Factor of the absorption of the segments of the large intestine, ka*f_area*f_ka_colon: the regional absorption profile of the substance, the value of its source Byon2018, not fitted.

Released by a capsule (Enterion) as a solution of 2.5 mg, apixaban gave an AUC(0-t) about 60 % lower in the distal small bowel and 84 % lower in the ascending colon than the oral solution, the relative AUC 0.40 and 0.16 (Byon2018, abstract; ELIQUIS NDA 202155, Clinical Pharmacology Review, study CV185007, Reference ID 3088157); the label: 'absorbed throughout the gastrointestinal tract with the distal small bowel and ascending colon contributing about 55% of apixaban absorption' (ELIQUIS US prescribing information, 12.3 Absorption). The distal small bowel is the lower ileum (ile2) of the library, the colon one factor of its segments (caecum to rectum, the group colon). The factors are derived with the model, not fitted: a solution of 2.5 mg put into the lumen of the lower ileum and of the colon ascendens gives the AUC of Carm_api relative to an oral solution of 0.40 and 0.16 with the factors 0.149 (lower ileum) and 0.0567 (colon) (regional_absorption.py of the model, which derives them again after a refit; test_the_regional_absorption_is_that_of_byon2018 of tests/models/test_apixaban.py), without them 0.99 and 0.93. The factors depend on the fitted absorption (ka_api, fabs_api, the efflux GU__APISEC_k), so they and the fit were iterated to a common point: the factors derived on the adopted fit give the same factors. The colon factor replaces the fitted f_ka_colon_api, which the data of the plasma did not determine (profile likelihood open towards 0).

comp:modelDefinition.name: Model for coagulation factors and readouts.

notes.body:
Model for coagulation factors and readouts.
The effects depend on the total concentration of apixaban in the arm vein plasma C_api (input port, Carm_api of the body), as the assays measure the total drug in a plasma sample: the anti-factor Xa activity is linear in the concentration, the INR and the prothrombin time (PT) rise linearly with the concentration relative to their baseline, the modified prothrombin time (mPT) and the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) follow an Emax model of the concentration relative to their baseline.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.
